title: project & switch-project — Project Switching Utilities
description: Two zsh utilities for fast keyboard-driven project switching. `project` is an interactive script that uses fzf to pick from all git repos under configured roots and prints the selected path. `switch-project` is a zsh function that calls `project`, then focuses an existing kitty window context and opens the appropriate IDE.

title: US-001: project — pick from cache with fzf
description:
As a developer, I want a standalone `project` script that picks a git project interactively with fzf and prints its path, so I can use it standalone or compose it with other tools.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `PROJECT_ROOTS` is read as a colon-separated list of paths; `~` is expanded to `$HOME`
- [ ] If `PROJECT_ROOTS` is unset or empty, print an error to stderr and exit 1
- [ ] If the cache exists, fzf is populated from it immediately (no scanning)
- [ ] If the cache does not exist, scan first (US-002 logic), write the cache, then launch fzf
- [ ] Projects currently open in kitty (matched by cwd) are listed first under an `Open` group header; all other projects appear under an `All` group header
- [ ] Group headers are non-selectable; selecting a project returns its absolute path regardless of group
- [ ] Projects are displayed in fzf; the cache stores absolute paths, labels shown in fzf are relative to the matched root (e.g. `owner/repo`)
- [ ] When running inside kitty with socket access, fzf runs in a new kitty tab; result communicated back via FIFO (matching the `web`/`note` pattern)
- [ ] Otherwise fzf runs inline
- [ ] The selected project's absolute path is printed to stdout
- [ ] If the user cancels fzf, print nothing and exit 0
- [ ] Optional query argument pre-fills the fzf search (e.g. `project myrepo`)
- [ ] Tests: `PROJECT_ROOTS` parsing with multiple roots, `~` expansion, error on unset `PROJECT_ROOTS`, cache path used when present, cold-start scan when cache absent, open projects appear before all others in list output

## Quality Gates
- [ ] `zsh tests/project-tests.zsh`
close_reason: Implemented project() function with fzf picker, cache, kitty integration, and group headers

title: US-002: project --refresh — scan and rebuild cache with progress
description:
As a developer, I want to explicitly refresh the project cache with a live progress indicator so that I can see scanning is working across 1900+ repos.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `project --refresh` scans all roots in `PROJECT_ROOTS` for git repos at depth 1 and depth 2
- [ ] While scanning, a live counter is printed to stderr on a single overwriting line: `Scanning... N repos found`
- [ ] The progress line is cleared cleanly (no leftover text) when scanning completes
- [ ] Results are written to `PROJECT_CACHE` (default: `~/.cache/project-roots`), one absolute path per line
- [ ] `PROJECT_CACHE` path is configurable via env var, with `~` expanded
- [ ] After writing the cache, the fzf picker launches as normal
- [ ] Scanning completes in under 2 seconds for 1900+ repos
- [ ] If a root directory does not exist, skip it with a warning to stderr
- [ ] Tests: repos found at depth 1 and depth 2, missing root skipped with warning, cache file written with correct content, `PROJECT_CACHE` env var respected

## Quality Gates
- [ ] `zsh tests/project-tests.zsh`

title: US-003: switch-project — focus existing kitty window
description:
As a developer, I want `switch-project` to find and focus an existing kitty window for the selected project so that I don't lose terminal state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Calls `project` to get a selected path; if no path returned, exit silently
- [ ] Queries `kitty @ ls` (JSON) with `jq` to find windows matching the project
- [ ] Matching tries cwd first: any window whose `cwd` is within the project directory
- [ ] Falls back to title match: any tab/window whose title contains the project basename
- [ ] If a match is found, focuses it via `kitty @ focus-window` or `kitty @ focus-tab`
- [ ] Brings kitty to the foreground with `osascript -e 'tell application "kitty" to activate'`
- [ ] Tests: cwd match found, title match found when cwd misses, no match returns empty, mock `kitty @ ls` JSON used throughout

## Quality Gates
- [ ] `zsh tests/project-tests.zsh`

title: US-004: switch-project — open or focus IDE when switching to existing kitty window
description:
As a developer, I want the appropriate IDE to open when I switch to an existing kitty window so that code and terminal are co-located.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Project type is detected by inspecting files in the project root:
  - `tspconfig.yaml` present → `code <path>`
  - `package.json` present (no `tspconfig.yaml`) → `code <path>`
  - `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, or `.idea/` present → `idea <path>`
  - No match → IDE step skipped silently
- [ ] TypeSpec is checked before TypeScript
- [ ] IDE command is run only when an existing kitty window was found and focused
- [ ] Tests: each project type detected correctly from temp directories, TypeSpec takes priority over TypeScript, unknown type produces no IDE command

## Quality Gates
- [ ] `zsh tests/project-tests.zsh`

title: US-005: switch-project — fall back to cd when no kitty window exists
description:
As a developer, I want `switch-project` to `cd` into the project directory when no kitty window already exists for it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] When no matching kitty window is found (or kitty is unavailable), `cd` into the project path
- [ ] Since `switch-project` is a shell function, `cd` directly affects the calling shell
- [ ] No IDE is opened in this path
- [ ] Tests: verify the cd path is taken when kitty matching returns empty, verify no IDE command is invoked in this path

## Quality Gates
- [ ] `zsh tests/project-tests.zsh`
